name: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)
lead: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a glycoprotein hormone made by the placenta after implantation, consisting of an alpha subunit shared with LH, FSH and TSH and a hormone-specific beta subunit. It sustains the corpus luteum and progesterone production in early pregnancy and is the basis of pregnancy tests [1][2][30]. Because it acts on the luteinizing hormone (LH) receptor, it is used as a prescription injectable to trigger ovulation in fertility treatment and to stimulate the testes in some men with low testosterone [1][3][4][30].

For appearance, the relevance runs through the testes. Men who take testosterone or anabolic steroids for muscle, leanness and a more masculine physique experience suppression of their own LH signal, which can shrink the testes and reduce sperm production. In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities hCG is discussed as an add-on that keeps testicular volume and fertility intact during such use, and it appears on some sports anti-doping lists for that reason [4][17][30][33]. Some forum posts go further and propose it for facial masculinity, penile growth or alongside growth hormone for height; no trial evidence was found for those uses [5][6][7].

The clinical literature supports hCG for inducing puberty and spermatogenesis in men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, and reviews list it among options for steroid-induced hypogonadism [8][9][32]. hCG has also had a separate public life as the centrepiece of the "hCG diet" proposed by Albert Simeons in the 1950s, a practice that regulators and medical bodies have addressed repeatedly [31].

paras: hCG is a glycoprotein of about 237 amino acids made mainly by the syncytiotrophoblast after implantation. Its alpha subunit matches those of LH, FSH and TSH, while the beta subunit is unique, and a carboxy-terminal peptide on the beta subunit gives it a longer half-life than LH [30]. In pregnancy it acts on ovarian LH/hCG receptors to keep the corpus luteum producing progesterone through the first trimester [30]. Levels rise after implantation and typically peak around weeks 8 to 11, which is why urine and blood tests detect it [30].

In men hCG stimulates Leydig cells in the testes to make testosterone, which in turn supports intratesticular testosterone and sperm production. When outside testosterone suppresses the pituitary, LH and FSH fall and the testes become less active; hCG substitutes for the missing LH signal [30][32]. Because the testes then produce more testosterone, some of it is converted to estradiol, which forum users discuss as a reason for monitoring hormones [5].

In assisted reproduction, hCG, urinary or recombinant, triggers final oocyte maturation, with ovulation occurring about 38 to 40 hours after injection and IVF retrieval scheduled around 34 to 36 hours [30]; trials compare the two forms and strategies to reduce ovarian hyperstimulation [10][11][12][13]. In men with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, testosterone alone promotes virilization but not fertility; gonadotropin therapy with hCG, often with FSH, usually yields enough sperm for conception though counts remain below normal [32]. A 2024 systematic review of 103 studies with 5,328 patients found that hCG was the most commonly used gonadotropin, in 93 studies [9]. Early-stage research has also tested hormonal stimulation of spermatogenesis in men with non-obstructive azoospermia [14]. hCG is also a tumor marker for gestational trophoblastic disease and germ cell tumors [15][30].

subs.h: Use with testosterone and anabolic steroids
paras: Wikipedia states that prolonged anabolic steroid use suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, causing testicular atrophy, reduced sperm production and infertility, and names hCG alongside clomifene as a testosterone-boosting therapy after short courses [33]. A 2014 review in Fertility and Sterility noted that symptomatic hypogonadism can follow anabolic steroid use, that management may include testosterone replacement, hCG and selective estrogen receptor modulators, and that no studies met the criteria for a formal meta-analysis [8]. A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized trials in functional hypogonadism found that clomiphene or enclomiphene raised testosterone, LH and FSH compared with placebo, and compared the SERMs and combined treatment with hCG [16].

Forum members on looksmax.org and T Nation say they use hCG to try to prevent testicular atrophy and protect fertility during testosterone use [17][18][19][20]. Wikipedia notes that men on testosterone replacement may also use hCG to preserve fertility and testicular size [30].

British endocrinologist Albert Simeons, practising in Rome, published Pounds and Inches in 1954, proposing low-dose hCG together with a diet of under about 500 calories per day, based on observations of pregnant women in India and of boys with Frohlich's syndrome [31]. A 1976 double-blind study in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition concluded hCG was no more effective than dietary restriction alone, and a 1995 meta-analysis by Lijesen and colleagues concluded that supporting studies were methodologically weak and that hCG did not produce weight loss, fat redistribution or reduced hunger [31].

The FDA required a disclaimer in 1976 that hCG is not approved for obesity; the FTC barred Kevin Trudeau from making hCG diet weight-loss claims in 2008; the FDA and FTC acted in December 2011 to remove homeopathic and over-the-counter hCG diet products from the market; and the American Medical Association adopted a policy in November 2016 that hCG for weight loss is inappropriate [30][31]. Wikipedia states that the consensus is that weight loss on these diets reflects the very low calorie intake, which carries malnutrition risk [31].

Randomized and observational studies of hCG address women's fertility treatment [10][11][12] and male hypogonadotropic hypogonadism [9]. A review of steroid-induced hypogonadism, which discusses hCG, found no study of sufficient quality for a meta-analysis [8]. A systematic review and meta-analysis of SERMs for male hypogonadism included comparisons against hCG [16]. A phase 1 trial enrolled 100 men with non-obstructive azoospermia in hormonal stimulation of spermatogenesis [14]. For weight loss, a 1976 double-blind trial and a 1995 meta-analysis are described above [31].
No clinical trial has tested hCG for facial masculinity, penile size or height in people without an endocrine disorder.

Wikipedia lists warnings for hCG including ectopic and multiple pregnancy, thromboembolic events, pregnancy loss, increased androgen production in males, and contraindication in androgen-dependent tumors [30]. Because hCG stimulates testicular testosterone and estrogen production, forum posters report the need to manage estradiol alongside it; a looksmax.org poster notes that hCG increases testosterone, which is converted to estradiol [5]. In fertility treatment, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome is a recognised complication, and trials examine ways to prevent it [13][21]. Posters on T Nation describe mixed experiences stopping hCG, including feeling worse after stopping and mood and weight changes after stopping an aromatase inhibitor and hCG [22][23].

In 1927 Selmar Aschheim and Bernhard Zondek developed a biological pregnancy test, the Aschheim-Zondek test, by detecting gonadotropic activity, later attributed to hCG, in the urine of pregnant women [1]. Rabbit-based and then immunological and radioimmunoassay methods followed in the 1930s, 1960 and 1970s [1]. An international unit for hCG was defined in 1938 [30]. Simeons published his diet in 1954 [31]. Recombinant gonadotropins, including hCG, were produced after the genes for the subunits were cloned [24].

In the US, hCG is a prescription-only injectable. Non-prescription products such as oral drops, pellets or sprays marketed for weight loss are not FDA-approved and are considered unapproved new drugs [1]. The FDA and FTC declared homeopathic and OTC hCG diet products fraudulent in 2011 [31]. A T Nation user reported that an endocrinologist prescribing testosterone would not also prescribe hCG, so he sourced it himself [19].

hCG is on some sports banned lists because it raises testosterone. Wikipedia cites suspensions including Manny Ramirez (50 MLB games, 2009), Brian Cushing (4 NFL games), Dennis Siver (UFC) and Jurickson Profar (80 games, 2025) [30][31].

On looksmax.org, hCG appears in threads about how long into a first testosterone cycle to start it, whether it is needed for a lower-dose cycle, and whether to run it long term with enclomiphene [17][18][25][26]. Other threads ask about using it with growth hormone for facial growth or height, with DHT gel for penile growth, or as a facial-masculinity tool [5][27][28][29]. Members dispute some of these claims in the threads themselves [5].

lore.intro: hCG is a staple of looksmax.org and T Nation conversation about testosterone and steroid use, usually as a way to keep testes active, and occasionally as a face, height or penis-growth tool [5][17][19][29].

claims.claim: hCG prevents testicular atrophy and preserves fertility on testosterone
claims.believers: Posters say its purpose is to maintain testicular function while LH and FSH signalling falls, best started alongside testosterone [17].
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes hCG use to preserve fertility and prevent testicular atrophy in men on testosterone therapy, and reviews describe it as a management option in steroid-induced hypogonadism, though a 2014 review found no quality studies for meta-analysis [30][8][9].

claims.claim: hCG is needed on a low-dose first cycle
claims.believers: One poster would add it to optimise a cycle; another said it is not necessary at low doses if finances do not allow [18].
claims.experts: No trials compare outcomes with and without hCG in recreational users.

claims.claim: hCG improves facial growth alongside growth hormone
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster suggested that people taking high growth hormone doses for bone and face growth should look into hCG, saying it may do more for facial growth than raising the dose; others in the thread objected [5].
claims.experts: No published studies have tested hCG for facial or bone growth in healthy people.

claims.claim: hCG, with or without DHT gel, can increase penis size
claims.believers: Threads ask whether to use hCG with DHT gel or alone for growth [28][29].
claims.experts: No study in typical men supports this; hormonal therapy for micropenis involves testosterone or DHT in defined disorders.

claims.claim: hCG can substitute for or improve on clomiphene-type recovery after a cycle
claims.believers: Threads discuss running hCG or enclomiphene long term [26].
claims.experts: A 2025 meta-analysis compared clomiphene or enclomiphene with hCG in male hypogonadism, and Wikipedia names hCG and clomifene as testosterone-boosting therapies after steroid courses [16][33].

claims.claim: Over-the-counter hCG diets cause weight loss
claims.believers: Simeons proposed in 1954 that hCG causes fat rather than lean loss on a very low-calorie diet; this is not a prominent claim on the forums reviewed [31].
claims.experts: A 1976 double-blind study and a 1995 meta-analysis found no benefit beyond calorie restriction, the FDA declared OTC hCG diet products fraudulent in 2011, and the AMA called hCG for weight loss inappropriate in 2016 [31][30].

card.summary: The pregnancy hormone that fertility clinics and TRT doctors use to keep testes working; forum claims for face, height and penis growth are untested.
card.note: Prescription-only injectable in the US; OTC hCG weight-loss products are unapproved.

quick.overview:
hCG is the hormone made by the placenta that pregnancy tests detect. It mimics luteinizing hormone, so doctors use it to trigger ovulation and to stimulate the testes in some men with hypogonadism.

In looksmaxxing circles it is mainly used by men on testosterone or steroids to keep testes working and fertility intact. Claims for facial growth, height or penis size have not been tested in trials.
quick.mechanism: hCG binds the luteinizing hormone receptor. In men this stimulates the testes to make testosterone and supports sperm production, which are otherwise suppressed when outside testosterone shuts down the pituitary signal.
quick.risks: It is a prescription injectable in the US; non-prescription hCG weight-loss products are unapproved. Because it raises testosterone and so estradiol, users report needing to monitor hormones. Ovarian hyperstimulation is a known complication in fertility treatment.
